title: Risk-Preserving Data Compression for Finite-Population ATE under Complete Balanced Assignment
banked_reason: Independent validity gate confirms honest below-field delivery: promised uniform W obstruction and first nonzero all-estimator compression-tax law remain unresolved; only finite certificates, inherited n=8 separation and an O(n^-4/3) envelope are established.
gap_reasons: The delivered note establishes finite decision certificates and a symmetry reduction, leaving the first nonzero all-estimator compression-tax asymptotics unresolved.

The sandwich imports the public [Sudijono et al. benchmark](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13822v1) and proves only an O(n^(-4/3)) upper envelope, with no eventual positivity, positive lower rate, evaluated limiting operator, or sharp attaining correction.

The promised first nonzero all-estimator asymptotic law for the fixed-half compression tax is replaced by a common-risk sandwich and an O(n^{-4/3}) upper envelope; it supplies neither an explicit tax normalization/positive limiting operator nor matched same-scale all-rule lower and attaining upper comparisons.
proof_attempt_summary: Three D0 solve rounds established finite compression-preservation/descent theory, the all-size preserving refinement (W,|V|), an inherited exact n=8 obstruction, and a first-order risk sandwich with an O(n^-4/3) compression-tax upper envelope. The accepted pivot promised strict W information loss for every even n>=8, but the proof supplies strictness only at eight; the original first nonzero all-estimator tax asymptotics and parity-correct two-sided transfer remain unresolved. D0.5 mathematical and citation audits passed, but the typed decision found kernel substitution and the general reviewer graded incremental (3.2 versus field floor); independent validity consultation confirmed no bounded repair, so the run was banked downgraded without Lean formalization.
tldr: Under fixed half treatment assignment and the entire deterministic binary schedule class, retaining \((W,|V|)\) preserves the original-record minimax squared-error risk for the finite-population ATE at every even size. An exact active-residual criterion tests preservation by other count statistics, and a positive LP margin gives a total estimator with certified improvement. The credited rational witness proves strict loss from retaining only \(W\) at \(n=8\). An additional risk sandwich gives both minimax risks the leading term \(1/n\), with deviations \(O(n^{-4/3})\), and bounds the tax above by \(C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). This envelope gives no positivity, positive lower rate, or first nonzero compression-tax equivalent; strictness at larger even sizes remains unresolved.
gap: A statistic may preserve worst-case ATE squared loss without preserving the entire experiment. Existing scalar minimax design results and the banked four-size calculation do not decide preservation of a general count reduction or rule out renewed preservation at larger exact-balance sizes.
fill: The reusable criterion is paired with a sample-size-uniform hypergeometric obstruction for the difference and a finite descent certificate. The contribution depends on deriving that obstruction on the full schedule lattice; the general convex equivalence and finite computation are supporting machinery.
